blocks.text: Lower Mary Hill Neighbourhood: streets and boundaries

items.t: Lower Mary Hill is the low, flat foot of Mary Hill: the Pitt River Road grid of Pooley Avenue, Morgan Avenue, Knappen Street, Humber Crescent, Western Drive and Eastern Drive, between Shaughnessy Street on the west and the Mary Hill Bypass on the east.

The east edge is a highway, not a street: the Mary Hill Bypass separates these lots from the Pitt River, and the City's floodplain map labels the bypass, the dike and the Fremont Connector across the low ground at the neighbourhood's east side.

The south edge is water: the Pitt River and Fraser River meet below the hill, and Colony Farm — now ƛ̓éxətəm Regional Park — sits across the Coquitlam River to the west, reached by the PoCo Climb trail and the Shaughnessy Street crossing.

blocks.text: Lower Mary Hill Neighbourhood: the housing stock

items.t: The pattern is post-war suburbia on the flat: the City's Housing Action Plan records that in the 1950s the older grid pattern "was replaced by a subdivision design creating larger lots fronting curvilinear streets and no lanes in the Lincoln Park and Mary Hill neighbourhoods" — Lower Mary Hill's curving Western Drive and Humber Crescent streets are that pattern, at the hill's foot.

blocks.text: Lower Mary Hill Neighbourhood: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Noise is a regulated condition at the bypass edge, not just a fact of life: the Harbour Street rezoning conditions required legal agreements for buildings "designed to incorporate recommendations of the Acoustical Evaluation and for the construction of a sound attenuation fence along Mary Hill Road."

The plan frame is the Official Community Plan Bylaw, 2013, No. 3838, which notes the Mary Hill Bypass and the Fraser River "help shape the distribution of land uses within the City" — the bypass corridor is a planned land-use edge, not an accident.

blocks.text: Lower Mary Hill Neighbourhood: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Kilmer Park at 1844 Pooley Avenue and Thompson Park at 1842 Morgan Avenue are the grid's two interior parks — both legal parcels assembled from the original subdivision lots, per the same 1977 park dedication bylaw's lot descriptions.

The trail under your feet is one named system: the Traboulay PoCo Trail rings the city along the Coquitlam, Pitt and Fraser rivers, and its Mary Hill section is the dike-top path the flood rules in the houses note close at high water — recreation and flood infrastructure are the same corridor here.
The hill above has a name for its top: Citadel Heights and Castle Park sit above Lower Mary Hill's east side — "lower" in the name is literal elevation against the Citadel slope, not a price label.

blocks.text: Lower Mary Hill Neighbourhood: development and new projects

items.t: PoCo Climb trail, Mary Hill to ƛ̓éxətəm Regional Park, City of Port Coquitlam: 6.5-kilometre loop with 200 timber stairs and a Shaughnessy Street crosswalk — status: completed, per the City's 2025 annual report highlights (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: Lower Mary Hill Neighbourhood: getting around

items.t: Route 159, Braid Station to Coquitlam Central Station, runs the Mary Hill Bypass and Shaughnessy Street at the neighbourhood's edges — the bus that drops riders at the Colony Farm / ƛ̓éxətəm Regional Park trail entrance at the bypass and Shaughnessy.

faq.a: Two School District No. 43 schools sit in or at the foot of Mary Hill: École Mary Hill Elementary, kindergarten to Grade 5, at 1890 Humber Crescent, and Kilmer Elementary, kindergarten to Grade 5, at 1575 Knappen Street. The houses note lists the middle and secondary schools (École Pitt River Middle, École Riverside Secondary); catchment for a specific address is confirmed in the SD43 School Locator, not by proximity.
faq.q: Which elementary schools are actually on this side of the hill?

faq.a: ƛ̓éxətəm Regional Park (formerly Colony Farm Regional Park) is a Metro Vancouver regional park on the Coquitlam River flats west of Shaughnessy Street — regional, not City, jurisdiction. What the City built is the connection: the PoCo Climb loop and the Shaughnessy Street crosswalk tie Mary Hill's streets into the regional park's trail system. Fremont Village, the newer development area across the Pitt River side of the city, is a different neighbourhood and its facts are not Lower Mary Hill facts.
faq.q: Is the big park across the river part of Port Coquitlam?

faq.a: In two documented ways. The Mary Hill Bypass is the neighbourhood's east boundary and its highway link toward Lougheed Highway and Highway 1, and the City has required a sound attenuation fence and acoustical design conditions for new building on the bypass-edge lands at Harbour Street.
